cc-01-c1.text: Daveed Vandevoorde (2005). Right Angle Brackets (N1757/05-0017). ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG21 C++ Standards Committee papers.
cc-01-c1.quote: The problem is an immediate consequence of the the “maximum munch” principle and the fact that >> is a valid token (right shift) in C++.
cc-01-c1.claim: The same rule made >> a long-standing problem in C++ template parsing.

cc-01-c3.text: Python Software Foundation (2026). Lexical analysis: Indentation. The Python Language Reference, docs.python.org.
cc-01-c3.quote: The indentation levels of consecutive lines are used to generate INDENT and DEDENT tokens, using a stack, as follows.
cc-01-c3.claim: Python's lexer tracks indentation levels on a stack and synthesizes virtual INDENT and DEDENT tokens.

cc-05-c3.text: Nada Amin, Ross Tate (2016). Java and Scala's Type Systems are Unsound: The Existential Crisis of Null Pointers. OOPSLA 2016 (ACM).
cc-05-c3.quote: We present short programs that demonstrate the unsoundness of Java and Scala's current type systems.
cc-05-c3.claim: the null-related holes Amin and Tate found in Java's and Scala's generics (2016)

cc-08-c2.text: Massimiliano Poletto, Vivek Sarkar (1999). Linear Scan Register Allocation. ACM Transactions on Programming Languages and Systems 21(5).
cc-08-c2.quote: This algorithm is not based on graph coloring, but allocates registers to variables in a single linear-time scan of the variables' live ranges.
cc-08-c2.claim: Linear scan (Poletto and Sarkar, 1999) sorts live ranges by start point and walks them in one pass, assigning registers as ranges become live and freeing them as ranges end.
